hints: Look at the sample: the first row of the answer is the first column of matrix. What happens to the shape — how many rows and how many columns does the answer have?
Create a new grid of size cols × rows and copy with the indices swapped: result[j][i] = matrix[i][j].

1. Let rows = matrix.length, cols = matrix[0].length.
  2. Create result with cols rows and rows columns.
  3. For every cell (i, j), set result[j][i] = matrix[i][j].
  4. Return result.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Build a new cols × rows grid with result[j][i] = matrix[i][j]. Every cell must be copied once, so this is the best possible.

explain: The sample is 2 × 3, so the answer is 3 × 2. Column 0 of the input is 1, 4, so the first answer row is [1, 4]; column 1 gives [2, 5] and column 2 gives [3, 6]. Every cell (i, j) moves to (j, i). The common mistake is assuming the grid is square and transposing in place — keep rows and cols separate and allocate a new grid.
recognize: "Row i of the answer is column i of the input" → swap the roles of the two indices.
javascript: function transpose(matrix) { const r = matrix.length, c = matrix[0].length; const out = []; for (let j = 0; j < c; j++) { const row = []; for (let i = 0; i < r; i++) row.push(matrix[i][j]); out.push(row); } return out; }
